newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes low, money rates end high.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes low, money rates end high.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed lower against the dollar on Friday but seasonal local demand pushed money rates up in the market, brokers said.
The rupee closed at 56.60 to the U.S. currency after opening at 56.50, they said. The currency closed at 56.52 on Thursday.
"(The dollar) came down to 56.42 in the morning. But it went up again when a big state bank began covering imports," a local bank dealer said.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by 1.25 local cents in response to the overseas strength of the U.S. unit, and fixed buying and selling prices at 56.0984 and 57.2317.
Overnight call money closed high at 26 percent after opening at 20, dealers said.

"The market is experiencing liquidity problems due to a lot of seasonal cash payments like bonuses and festival payments," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer. "The shortage is pushing money rates up."
He said there were a lot of transactions to generate rupees as dealers began swapping for the local currency.
"The money market will remain high till early January because of this seasonal demand for rupees," he said.
